panels.title: Completed deliveries (range)
panels.description: Delivery attempts that ended in completed status in the last hour (notifications_deliveries_total). Computed over the time range selected in Grafana ($__range) and the client filter; recalculated when the range or client changes.

panels.title: Failed deliveries (range)
panels.description: Delivery attempts that ended in failed status in the last hour (notifications_deliveries_total). Computed over the time range selected in Grafana ($__range) and the client filter; recalculated when the range or client changes.

panels.title: Success rate (range)
panels.description: Completed over final outcomes (completed + failed) in the selected range. notifications_deliveries_total counts state transitions, so retrying transitions are excluded: an event that fails after five attempts counts once as failed, not five times.

panels.title: Webhook latency p95 (range)
panels.description: 95th percentile of the client webhook POST duration in the last hour, across all clients (notifications_webhook_latency_seconds). Computed over the time range selected in Grafana ($__range) and the client filter; recalculated when the range or client changes.

panels.title: Overdue backlog (worker)
panels.description: Current value of the gauge; does not depend on the time range.

panels.title: Events by status (Postgres)
panels.description: Current state of the notification_events table according to postgres_exporter. It is a point-in-time snapshot; it does not depend on the time range or the client filter.

panels.title: Duplicates (range)
panels.description: Received events that already existed (same idempotency key) in the last hour (notifications_duplicates_total). Computed over the time range selected in Grafana ($__range) and the client filter; recalculated when the range or client changes.

panels.title: Skipped (range)
panels.description: Received events that the service decided not to record in the last hour (notifications_skipped_total): e.g. no active subscription for the event_key. Computed over the time range selected in Grafana ($__range) and the client filter; recalculated when the range or client changes.

panels.title: Backends by state
panels.description: pg_stat_activity_count{datname="notifications"} by state (active, idle, idle in transaction, ...). Open sessions by state; many sustained 'idle in transaction' sessions indicate clients that open transactions and never close them.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit[5m]) and rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback[5m]) for the notifications database.

panels.title: Tuples per second
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_tup_returned|tup_fetched|tup_inserted|tup_updated|tup_deleted[5m]) for the notifications database: how many rows Postgres processes per second, the most direct signal of workload.

panels.title: Blocks read: disk vs. cache per second
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_blks_read[5m]) (disk) and rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit[5m]) (buffer cache) for the notifications database. See also 'Cache hit ratio' in this row for the proportion.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Proportion of blocks served from Postgres's buffer cache over the total read (pg_stat_database_blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read)) for the notifications database.

panels.title: I/O time (read/write)
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_blk_read_time[5m]) and rate(pg_stat_database_blk_write_time[5m]) for the notifications database, in ms of I/O per wall-clock second. Requires track_io_timing=on in Postgres; in this stack track_io_timing is OFF (pg_settings_track_io_timing=0), so both series stay at 0 even when there is real I/O — the panel measures nothing until that setting is enabled.

panels.title: Average busy sessions (database load)
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_active_time_seconds_total[5m]): seconds of SQL execution per second summed across all sessions, i.e. the average number of sessions running queries. 1 = one session busy the whole time; above the VM's number of cores, the database is saturated (PostgresBusyBackendsAboveCores alert).

panels.title: Longest running transaction
panels.description: pg_stat_activity_max_tx_duration{datname="notifications"}: duration in seconds of the oldest currently open transaction. A long transaction holds locks and blocks autovacuum.

panels.title: Temp files/bytes per second
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_database_temp_bytes[5m]) (bytes/s) and rate(pg_stat_database_temp_files[5m]) (files/s) for the notifications database: how much sorting/hashing is spilling to disk because it doesn't fit in work_mem. Two different units on the same panel (bytes/s and files/s), identified in the legend; if they grow together, raise work_mem or review the query plan.

panels.title: Checkpoints per second
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_bgwriter_checkpoints_timed_total[5m]) (time-based, checkpoint_timeout) vs. rate(pg_stat_bgwriter_checkpoints_req_total[5m]) (forced, e.g. by max_wal_size). Many sustained 'req' checkpoints indicate max_wal_size is too small for the write rate.

panels.title: Buffers written: backend vs. checkpointer
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_bgwriter_buffers_backend_total[5m]) (a backend had to write its own dirty buffer, a sign the checkpointer/bgwriter can't keep up) vs. rate(pg_stat_bgwriter_buffers_checkpoint_total[5m]) (written in an orderly way by the checkpointer).

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: pg_database_size_bytes{datname="notifications"}: total on-disk size of the notifications database.

panels.title: Scans per table: index vs. sequential
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan[5m]) vs. rate(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan[5m]) for notification_events and delivery_attempts. A high, sustained seq_scan on delivery_attempts indicates the partial index on due attempts is not being used (check the plan with EXPLAIN).

panels.title: Delivery rate by status
panels.description: Delivery attempts per second, grouped by final status (notifications_deliveries_total). Filterable by client_id.

panels.title: Webhook latency p50/p95/p99 by client
panels.description: Percentiles of the webhook POST duration, by client (notifications_webhook_latency_seconds).

panels.title: Failures by client
panels.description: Rate of delivery attempts in failed status, by client (notifications_deliveries_total).

panels.title: Worker backlog vs. Postgres
panels.description: Compares each worker's in-memory gauge (max(notifications_attempts_due)) with the direct count in Postgres (cobre_attempts_due, item 2 of the brief); if they diverge a lot, the worker's gauge is stale.

panels.title: Age of oldest pending item
panels.description: Seconds elapsed since next_attempt_at of the oldest due, unexecuted attempt (cobre_oldest_pending_age_seconds); 0 if none is pending.

panels.title: Worker batch rate
panels.description: Scheduling ticks processed per second by the worker (notifications_batches_total); each batch claims up to 50 attempts.

panels.title: Claimed unfinished attempts
panels.description: Attempts with claimed_at but no executed_at in Postgres (cobre_attempts_claimed_unfinished); if it grows steadily, a worker died holding the lease.

panels.title: Event registration rate
panels.description: New events recorded per second, by client (notifications_registered_total).

panels.title: Skipped events
panels.description: Received events that the service decided not to record (notifications_skipped_total), exactly as the counter exposes it (no window aggregation).

panels.title: Duplicates (range)
panels.description: Events with a repeated idempotency key in the selected time range (increase over $__range); these are queue redeliveries that are discarded without touching the database.

panels.title: (note)
panels.description: Note on the ElasticMQ observability limitation described in the brief (item 3) and in the README.

options.content: **ElasticMQ queue depth for `account-events` is not instrumented.** ElasticMQ does not expose its own Prometheus endpoint. As a proxy, the rate of `notifications_registered_total` is used (panel on the left): a registration rate that doesn't grow with load suggests messages are piling up in the queue before reaching the worker. See `deploy/local/README.md`, section "What isn't instrumented", for the alternative that was evaluated and not applied.

panels.title: Error log rate by job
panels.description: rate(logback_events_total{level="error"}[5m]) grouped by job (api/worker). The NotificationsErrorLogRateHigh alert fires on this same signal above 0.5/s over 5 minutes.

panels.title: Warning log rate by job
panels.description: rate(logback_events_total{level="warn"}[5m]) grouped by job; it does not trigger any alert, it is context signal.

panels.title: Worker scheduler errors
panels.description: increase(notifications_scheduler_errors_total[5m]): failures claiming or scheduling a batch of attempts, distinct from an individual delivery failure.

panels.title: API 5xx responses by uri
panels.description: rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{status=~"5.."}[5m]) grouped by uri; feeds the NotificationsApiServerErrors alert (>1% of requests over 5 minutes).

panels.title: HikariCP pool timeouts
panels.description: increase(hikaricp_connections_timeout_total[5m]) by job: requests that failed to get a pool connection in time.

panels.title: Longest GC pauses
panels.description: jvm_gc_pause_seconds_max by job/instance: the longest garbage collection pause observed since the process last restarted.

panels.title: RPS by uri and status
panels.description: sum by (uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[1m])) for notifications-api.

panels.title: p95 by uri
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95, ...) over http_server_requests_seconds_bucket. Needs the buckets enabled in application.yaml (management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram, item 1 of the brief); without restarting the service with that change, this series has no data because http_server_requests_seconds_bucket does not exist yet.

panels.title: 4xx vs 5xx
panels.description: Rate of client errors (4xx) vs. server errors (5xx) from notifications-api.

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: sum(http_server_requests_active_seconds_count): number of HTTP requests currently in flight in notifications-api.

panels.title: Heap used vs. max
panels.description: jvm_memory_used_bytes{area="heap"} and jvm_memory_max_bytes{area="heap"} by job/memory pool id (Eden, Survivor, Tenured).

panels.title: GC pauses: rate and max
panels.description: rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum[5m]) (time paused per wall-clock second) and jvm_gc_pause_seconds_max, by job.

panels.title: Live threads
panels.description: jvm_threads_live_threads by job/instance.

panels.title: Process and system CPU
panels.description: process_cpu_usage (fraction of CPU used by the JVM) and system_cpu_usage (fraction of CPU used by the whole container system), by job.

panels.title: HikariCP active/idle/pending/max
panels.description: hikaricp_connections_{active,idle,pending,max}, by job/instance. Sustained pending>0 triggers NotificationsDbPoolExhausted.

panels.title: Acquisition time (max)
panels.description: hikaricp_connections_acquire_seconds_max, by job/instance. The endpoint does not publish buckets for this histogram today, so the max is used instead of a percentile.

panels.title: Active connections in Postgres
panels.description: pg_stat_database_numbackends for the notifications database, via postgres-exporter.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: pg_stat_database_deadlocks for the notifications database; should always be 0.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: pg_locks_count for the notifications database, grouped by lock mode.

panels.title: pg_up
panels.description: pg_up: 1 if postgres-exporter successfully connected to Postgres on the last scrape, 0 otherwise. Feeds the PostgresDown alert.

panels.title: Inserts/updates by table
panels.description: rate(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_ins[5m]) and rate(pg_stat_user_tables_n_tup_upd[5m]) for notification_events and delivery_attempts.

panels.title: Dead tuples
panels.description: pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup for notification_events and delivery_attempts; if it grows without autovacuum bringing it down, it indicates autovacuum can't keep up.

panels.title: Table size on disk
panels.description: pg_stat_user_tables_table_size_bytes for notification_events and delivery_attempts.

panels.title: Total CPU by mode (%)
panels.description: sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total[5m])) / scalar(count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"})): fraction of the VM's total CPU capacity (all cores) used in each mode (user, system, iowait, idle, ...) per second (the scalar() is needed because count() without 'by' produces a series with no labels, which otherwise wouldn't match the per-mode series). Feeds HostCpuSaturated (idle < 10%). Postgres's internal load (active time, backends by state, transactions/tuples per second, block I/O) is read in the 'Postgres load' row, not here: node_exporter does not distinguish processes, only the whole VM. CPU/memory for the Postgres container specifically is not observable from inside this stack: under OrbStack no container can reach the Docker socket (not root, not privileged, not even mounting /var/run: 'permission denied'), and cAdvisor (which doesn't need the socket) doesn't work here either because this daemon uses the containerd snapshotter, which its v0.52.1 doesn't support for resolving a container's layer. To see per-container CPU/memory (including postgres), use `docker stats --no-stream` on the host.

panels.title: Load average vs. available cores
panels.description: node_load1/5/15 for the VM, overlaid with count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}) (number of cores) as a reference: if sustained load exceeds the number of cores, there is more work ready to run than CPU to handle it.

panels.title: Memory used vs. total (VM)
panels.description: node_memory_MemTotal_bytes - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes (used, includes reclaimable page cache) against node_memory_MemTotal_bytes (total assigned to the Docker VM). Feeds HostMemoryLow (available < 10%).

panels.title: Disk I/O: bytes read/written by device
panels.description: rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total[5m]) and rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total[5m]), by device (vda/vdb are the VM's real disks on this host; nbd* are unused network-block devices, normally at 0).

panels.title: Disk I/O: io_time by device
panels.description: rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total[5m]): fraction of each second the device had at least one I/O operation in flight (0 to 1, can approach 1 with deep queues even without much throughput). Complements the bytes-read/written panel.

panels.title: Network by interface
panels.description: rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total[5m]) and rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total[5m]), by the VM's network interface.

panels.title: Disk space (VM)
panels.description: node_filesystem_avail_bytes and node_filesystem_size_bytes. The VM's "/" mountpoint does not show up in node_exporter: its real fstype falls in the filesystem collector's default exclusion list (typically 'overlay' on an OrbStack VM's rootfs). /var/lib/docker is used as a proxy — the same physical device (/dev/vdb1) as the rest of the VM's data disk — to get a real free-space signal.

panels.title: JVM process CPU
panels.description: process_cpu_usage{job=~"notifications-api|notifications-worker"}: fraction of CPU used by each JVM process (api, worker), by instance. Unlike the VM CPU above, this one is per process — Micrometer reports it from inside each JVM, without depending on cAdvisor or the Docker socket.

panels.title: Approximate JVM RSS memory
panels.description: sum by (job) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job=~"notifications-api|notifications-worker"}): sum of all JVM memory areas (heap + non-heap) reported by Micrometer, by job. It is an approximation of the process's real RSS (the OS's RSS also includes native memory outside the JVM's accounting: native thread stacks, library mmaps, direct buffers not always included), but it is the closest per-process signal available without access to the process's /proc from inside this stack.
